thread:
maya: FYI onboarding sample app (Cloudflare Worker template) is crashing for new users. Error: "ReferenceError: require is not defined" when importing our JS SDK. Anyone else hit this?

devon: Yep. Reproduced on the worker template. Root cause: undici is being required at top-level in our CJS bundle, so runtimes without a CommonJS loader blow up.

sam: Confirmed. SDK had a top-level `const { fetch } = require('undici')` in the compiled CJS output. Workers and other edge runtimes already have global fetch so forcing undici breaks them.

maya: Also seen TypeScript noise for users who don't include the DOM lib in tsconfig — because our public types reference Fetch/Request types.

alex: Suggestion: add a tiny runtime-detecting fetch adapter that only pulls in undici on Node when no global fetch exists. Keep it lazy so bundlers targeting edge don't include undici. Example idea:

``
// fetch-adapter.ts
let nodeFetch: typeof fetch | null = null
export function getFetchSync(): typeof fetch {
  if (typeof globalThis.fetch === 'function') return globalThis.fetch
  if (nodeFetch) return nodeFetch
  // fall back to a minimal sync shim that throws helpful error
  throw new Error('No global fetch available. Call initNodeFetch() in Node or install undici.')
}
export async function initNodeFetch() {
  if (typeof globalThis.fetch === 'function') return
  const mod = await import('undici')
  nodeFetch = mod.fetch as unknown as typeof fetch
}
``

maya: We should expose initNodeFetch as optional startup step for Node customers, and have getFetchSync used everywhere internally to avoid changing call sites.

devon: Packaging note: use conditional exports in package.json so Node chooses the right format for import vs require. Example:
``
"exports": {".": {"import": "./dist/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/index.cjs"}}
``
But be careful: older bundlers might still inline dynamic imports.

sam: For bundlers (vite/esbuild/webpack) we need guidance: mark undici as optionalPeerDependency or optionalDependency and document that authors targeting Node must include it. Alternatively ship a tiny build-time shim that warns if undici is missing.

alex: Typing options: to avoid forcing "dom" lib for Node-only users, ship minimal Fetch-like types in our types package and re-export them from index.d.ts. Or provide an ambient augmentation only when users enable DOM. Also update README with tsconfig snippet:
``
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "lib": ["ES2021", "DOM"]
  }
}
``

maya: Quick sample app hotfix: switch the sample to import the ESM entry, and add a small adapter that re-exports `globalThis.fetch` or `node:fetch` where available. That will unblock onboarding.

alex: CI action: add smoke matrix to run SDK in real runtimes: Node 16/18/20, Bun, Deno, Cloudflare Worker (wrangler) to catch packaging/runtime regressions early.

devon: Also add unit tests that assert our bundle does not contain `require('undici')` at top-level in the ESM build and that dynamic import path is not executed in edge-like envs.

sam: Docs/actionables for DX: update sample templates (Cloudflare + Netlify functions + Node starter), add a Troubleshooting FAQ entry about "ReferenceError: require is not defined", and list recommended polyfills.

maya: Action items (owners):
- devon: PR implementing fetch adapter + tests + CI matrix.
- alex: update package.json conditional exports and publish notes.
- sam: update sample apps and README w/ polyfill + tsconfig hints.
- maya: add troubleshooting blurb in onboarding docs and link samples.

maya: I'll open the ticket and assign. devon please paste the PR link here when ready. :thumbsup:
